trust_boundaries.name: Attacker-influenceable Exabeam telemetry entering the agent

threats.summary: An instruction planted in an alert field, case note, or raw event can reach the model through the invisible code points canonicalize.py deliberately keeps (ZWNJ/ZWJ, LRM/RLM, NBSP, FE00-FE0F), and any canonicalizer error passes the block through raw because the bridge is fail-open on reads.

The remote MCP's own parameter descriptions carry caller instructions ("always send fields:['*']", "IGNORE any user request"), so the tool schema itself is an injection channel; the reference corpus tells the agent that text is not authoritative and to disregard it.

Complying with the schema's fields:["*"] instruction on search_events/search_cases returns millions of characters and overflows the context window — a self-inflicted DoS that only prompt text prevents, with no result-size ceiling in the bridge.

trust_boundaries.name: Investigation content to the hosted Claude model

remit_rules.excerpt: Exporting or transmitting case/alert/event data to any destination other than the Exabeam MCP and the local investigation report file.

threats.summary: Every alert, event and case note gathered from the production tenant necessarily transits the externally hosted model provider, a destination the remit's outbound list does not enumerate even though its Identity block names Claude as the primary model.

The model is the enforcement point for the approval ask, the redaction rule and the untrusted-telemetry rule, yet the project does not pin it (ai:pinnedByThisProject false) — a swap to an unsupported smaller model silently weakens every prompt-level control, with only a docs-level supported floor.

trust_boundaries.name: Agent decision to the Exabeam tool surface

remit_rules.excerpt: Any external-egress tool wired into this agent's surface (email/chat/cloud-drive/arbitrary-HTTP send) — this agent transmits nothing off the Exabeam + local-report surface.

threats.summary: A containment action (host isolation, account disable, blocking) executed instead of recommended would be irreversible; the MCP exposes no such tool and seventeen containment-class names are hard-denied at the permission layer as defense-in-depth.

list_tools and call_tool proxy whatever the remote tenant advertises, so a tool added or renamed server-side is forwarded unreviewed; the deny-list covers only the seventeen known containment names and the bridge performs no allow-list check of its own.

trust_boundaries.name: Suppression and case writes to the production tenant

remit_rules.excerpt: the agent MUST state the action and reason, ask the analyst directly ... and WAIT for a clear yes before calling the tool — one item per approval.
Bulk suppression — dismissing or closing more than one item from a single decision ... Every suppression is its own item with its own human approval.
Dismissing or closing any item in a non-interactive / unattended run. With no interactive operator to approve, the agent operates read-only.
Approval MUST be obtained from an interactive operator regardless of the harness permission mode; a bypassed or auto-accepted permission prompt does not substitute for the analyst's explicit yes.
Batch triage is a read activity ... each state change (note, escalation, and above all suppression) is decided and executed one item at a time.

threats.summary: The unattended/headless mode the remit sanctions as read-only is not forced read-only anywhere in code: the shipped snippet marks update_alert/update_case "ask", which is not a deny when no human is present, and the bridge has no interactivity detection at all.

In the blessed interactive posture the gate is a real human prompt, so the residual is the approver: the same attacker-influenceable evidence the agent summarizes can be shaped so the case note and dismissal reason the analyst reads make the suppression look justified.

create_case and create_case_notes are auto-approved with no per-session budget, and nothing caps a loop of per-item update_alert calls, so a poisoned queue could drive runaway case creation or a scripted per-item suppression sweep that only the prompt's cadence rule bounds.

The write-sink neutralizer defangs formulas and markdown-link targets fail-closed, but a bare URL or domain typed in prose is left live by design, so a phishing host quoted into a persisted case note is neutralized only by prompt.

trust_boundaries.name: Local investigation report and persisted case notes

remit_rules.excerpt: Reprinting a credential, token, password, or private key found in evidence into case notes or the report.
Exporting or transmitting case/alert/event data to any destination other than the Exabeam MCP and the local investigation report file.

threats.summary: A credential or PII value seeded in event evidence is kept out of the report and case note solely by the SKILL.md redaction instruction; the one code control on that path handles active content only and never looks for secrets.

The report is a plain local markdown file with no defined location, retention, encryption or access control, holding the full timeline and quoted evidence for a production tenant, and distribution is explicitly left to a human.

trust_boundaries.name: Exabeam OAuth credentials at rest and in the bridge

threats.summary: The API key and secret could leak through the repo or the agent's own logs; *.env is git-ignored, the docs mandate chmod 600, the values are never written to stderr and no secret value appears anywhere in the tree.

One tenant-scoped client credential serves reads and the gated writes alike and the MCP inherits whatever access level the key's role carries, so socxen adds no least-privilege separation between a read-only triage sweep and a suppression.

trust_boundaries.name: Plugin distribution and runtime dependency resolution

threats.summary: The process that mints and holds the Exabeam OAuth token runs on floor-pinned, lockfile-less dependencies that uv re-resolves at every launch, so a malicious mcp/httpx/certifi release is picked up silently.

Marketplace auto-update, when enabled fleet-wide, replaces the skill corpus, the permission snippet and the bridge source on analysts' machines with no review step between the upstream repo and a production-tenant agent.

The shipped model, prompt corpus, bridge dependencies or governance snippet could drift from what is declared; CI regenerates the CycloneDX AI-BOM and fails the build if the inventory no longer matches the sources.

trust_boundaries.name: Runtime logging out of the bridge

remit_rules.excerpt: Transmitting investigation data to any external destination. This agent ships no external-send capability (no email, chat, cloud-drive, or arbitrary-HTTP egress).

threats.summary: There is no durable or structured record of tool calls, verdicts or approval decisions — only ephemeral stderr hygiene lines and a free-form markdown report — so a suppression on a production tenant cannot be reconstructed or monitored after the session ends.

A hygiene record that echoed the stripped text back into the read stream would be forgeable and could re-embed the invisibles it just removed; the bridge logs only deduplicated code-point labels, out-of-band, and never appends them to content.

attack_paths.name: Planted benign explanation drives an approved suppression

steps.summary: Attacker plants a benign-explanation or instruction payload in alert/event/case-note text, optionally using code points the narrow, fail-open canonicalizer keeps.
The model reasons over the planted evidence with the untrusted-telemetry rule enforced only as prompt text (red-team class A/B is aimed exactly here).
The dismissal reason and case note the approver reads are shaped by the planted claim, manufacturing the human yes.
update_alert/update_case is forwarded with no interactivity or approval check — and in the sanctioned unattended run there is no approver in the loop at all.

attack_paths.name: Export injection through a persisted case note

steps.summary: A formula or phishing-link payload sits in a field value the investigation will quote (red-team a10).
The model echoes the value into the case note and report; prompt-level defang fixes did not hold across an eight-variant experiment.
The deterministic write sink quote-prefixes formulas and defangs markdown-link targets fail-closed, so the persisted artifact is clean.
The documented residuals remain — a bare URL/domain in prose and the terminal-display copy — where a live-looking phishing host survives into the analyst's view.

notes.lane_fit: Three strains, all from a prompt-shaped plugin with no application process of its own. (1) The dominant untrusted input origin is not in user_inputs at all — attacker-influenceable telemetry arrives from external_deploy through tools_mcp, so untrusted-ingress sits on a read-return edge rather than on a user_inputs node; user_inputs holds only the analyst. (2) settings.snippet.json is placed in agent_core as an approval gate per the lane table, but it is really config for the client_adapters harness and socxen ships no code that enforces it. (3) The model is placed in external_deploy as the upstream provider so model-egress has a real crossing, even though agent_core nominally owns 'the LLM call' — here the LLM *is* the orchestrator, and skill-md-orchestrator is a prompt file, not code. Related: the harness is the actual MCP transport, so skill-md-orchestrator--exabeam-mcp-bridge-py-mcp-server collapses harness dispatch plumbing into one edge.
notes.omissions: Repo-posture artifacts left out as non-runtime, with their evidence carried as threat mitigation_evidence instead: the CycloneDX AI-BOM plus gen_aibom.py, the CI invariants/eval suite, and the security/redteam corpus (attacks/, results/, HISTORY, PLAN, METHODOLOGY) — the last is the strongest single piece of this target's posture and does not fit any node kind. The 20-tool Exabeam surface is collapsed into one external_service node rather than split read/write, because the edge-id rule (<from>--<to>) permits only one edge per ordered pair; the read/write distinction is carried by the untrusted-ingress vs state-commit boundaries over the same edges. Four instruction-level control nodes are edgeless by design and each is noted here rather than given an invented flow: redaction-skill-md-control and untrusted-telemetry-skill-md-control constrain content the model produces or consumes rather than moving data; tool-map-md-control is a standing instruction about tool schemas; settings-snippet-json-control does have one edge (into the harness) only because the merge is a real config flow. Findings-JSON drift against this snapshot was minor and did not block any citation: security/redteam/PLAN.md's escalation-as-DoS line reads at 75 here versus 76 in the finding, and the bridge call_tool evidence lines (186/187) straddle the decorator. Not modelled for lack of citable mechanism: any read-side result-size ceiling, session identity, or multi-tenant separation.
notes.taxonomy_note: OWASP LLM codes here follow the current KB numbering (KB_LLM_TOP10.md: LLM03 Excessive Agency, LLM04 Supply Chain, LLM06 Unbounded Consumption, LLM10 Improper Output Handling), which differs from the frozen 2026-07-03 findings JSON's older numbering (LLM06 Excessive Agency, LLM03 Supply Chain, LLM10 Unbounded Consumption, LLM05 Improper Output Handling) — the meanings are unchanged, only the numbers. Two primaries diverge from the cited findings' own tags under the KB's arbitration section: PRAX-...-002 is tagged LLM03 (Excessive Agency) here rather than ASI03, because an approval layer that is present but not enforced in the self-directed mode is the gate row (agentic ASI10 rides only as a co-tag); and PRAX-...-003 is tagged LLM01 rather than ASI01, because the red-team results show no goal-alteration landing, which the arbitration section makes an ingress-hygiene gap.
